readability.summary: Every module of core/state opens with its purpose, boundaries and sources; every public item is documented, as the lints require; comments say why a rule exists and cite it; tests name the behaviour they prove. Review against the final code made the outbox report a negative stored time as an integrity error instead of reading a wrong time, recorded the previous session under explicit names instead of a debug rendering, and corrected a doc comment. The tests found two rules the code now states: the restart rules apply on every open, and a wall clock that moved back can neither settle an effect before it started nor stop the store from opening (TASK-008_EVIDENCE.md section 9).

cleanup.summary: TASK-008 created no temporary artifact inside the checkout: Cargo built into /mnt/F/Nexees-toolchains/target/; the tests' stores lived in the system temporary folder, each removed when its test ended; the negative-test copies and the lockfile regeneration used the session scratch folder; and every Python command that imports a module of the checkout ran with -B, so no bytecode was written there. At close, scripts/test/task_cleanup.py ran on the checkout with an empty TASK-008 manifest, first as a plan and then with --apply and its record: it removed nothing, refused nothing, and left in place 15 untracked files, all TASK-008 deliverables and evidence, each with its hash. The ignored files are the owner's IDE output (rust-analyzer's target/ and the Java extension's .gradle/ beside TASK-003's prototype); they are not task-owned and were left exactly as they are. The session scratch folder outside the checkout is removed once this receipt is committed and pushed. No pre-existing or user-owned file was deleted, reset or stashed.
